newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, focus on spreads.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, focus on spreads.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Wednesday, with gold finally climbing out of a four-day losing streak.

"We saw some trade buying near recent support levels, then locals went long and funds did some short covering, but about a quarter of the day's estimated volume of 43,000 lots in gold was in spreads, with the market focusing on the December/February roll ahead of the first delivery day next Wednesday for the December contract," Pell Brothers floor trader Don Tierney said.
In addition, some traders are covering short positions ahead of the OTC option expiry next Wednesday and the U.S. Thanksgiving Holiday next Thursday, traders said.
NYMEX and its COMEX division will be closed Nov 28 and 29.
A weak dollar in the wake of a larger-than-expected U.S. September trade deficit provided some support for precious metals, analysts said.
COMEX December gold closed up $0.60 at $379.00 an ounce after finding support again near a life-of-contract low of $377.80 which was set recently.
Spot gold in the bullion market closed at $378.20/80 versus the London afternoon fix of $379.10 and Tuesday's New York close of $377.85/378.35.
But gold fundamentals remain weak, analysts said.
World gold demand slipped two percent in the third quarter 1996 to 654.8 tonnes, while demand year-to-date is down four percent at 1,566 tonnes compared to 1995, World Gold Council said today.

The most significant drop came in investment demand in Japan which plunged 61 pct to 51.1 tonnes in the first nine months this year, compared to last year, as the slide in the yen pushed up gold prices in yen terms.
Meanwhile, official sector gold holdings, as published by the IMF, showed a net fall of 970,000 ounces (30.2 tonnes) in the third quarter.

The market has been concerned about likely European central bank gold sales, ahead of the introduction of Europe's single currency in 1999, as well as a proposed sale of five million ounces of gold by the IMF.

But in third-quarter 1996, the largest official sales were by South Africa, which reduced its gold reserves by 19.6 tonnes, as the South African rand slumped and the price of gold in rand reached a multi-year high oround 1800 rand.
December silver ended up 7.2 cents at $4.945 after trading from $4.865 to $4.965.

"Silver prices seem to be firmly positioned between support at $4.77 and resistance at $5.04," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said. "But with the first delivery day for the December contract scheduled for Nov 27, an upward push on prices is possible."
NYMEX January platinum closed up $1.70 at $388.00 and December palladium gained $0.65 to $119.75.
The April 1997 platinum/gold spread recovered further to close at $8.60 an ounce, its highest level since early September.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
